tasks.task: Fact-check a draft claim by claim before it is published

items.when: When a draft with facts, numbers, rankings or quotes is ready to publish or send
When each claim in an article, deck or report must be checked against its source
First, to list every claim that needs a source, ranked by risk
When the draft persuades, to sort each line into fact, inference or opinion
When one claim matters a lot, to build an evidence table with conflicts and gaps
When the writer gave no sources, to check each claim against trusted ones
When the writer gave sources, to tie each fact to one or mark it for rewrite or cut

tasks.task: Write a literature review on one question

items.when: When a decision waits on what the studies say and the review needs a plan
When one question must be answered from a body of studies
When the papers are not yet in hand and must be found in free databases
When you need sources chosen by clear rules and their findings pulled together
When the client needs a search others can repeat, with screening shown step by step
When the review is drafted, to map shared findings, conflicts and open questions
When the review is tidy because the studies that do not fit were left out

tasks.task: Summarise one paper in plain words with its limits

items.when: When a business reader needs the question, method, findings and strength of one paper
When the paper is a PDF with tables that must be read exactly
When you want key findings and plain summaries for several papers at once
When one concept blocks the reader and needs an everyday analogy with its limits
Before the summary goes out, to grade the study's design, bias and statistics
When the summary repeats the paper's jargon and you could not explain it to a friend

tasks.task: Write a short cited answer to one question

items.when: When there is one question and a set of sources or web search to answer it from
When you need a first pass on the web with source links you can open and check
When the answer must come from primary sources and be saved with them
When the fact sits in a public database and must be pulled the same way each time
When every claim must carry a source or be marked unsourced after repeated checks

tasks.task: Build an evidence table from a set of sources

items.when: When several papers or reports must sit side by side with the same fields
When each row needs the claim, the numbers and the limits taken from the full paper
When the table needs more sources, to gather current and competing findings on the topic

tasks.task: Check the strengths and limits of one study

items.when: When a writer or marketer wants to use a study and asks how strong it is
When all you have is a news item, to see what the study behind it really shows
When the full paper is in hand and needs a claim check and a methods review
When the result rests on a test or a small sample you are unsure how to read
When an impressive number may come from who was selected or how the chart is scaled
When a relative risk needs putting into numbers people can picture

tasks.task: Explain why sources disagree and which to trust

items.when: When two reports give different answers or numbers on the same question
When the sources are full papers and you need a claims table and a disagreement map
When the same set of papers will be compared again as new ones arrive
When the pile is mixed articles and reports and you need what is backed and what is disputed

tasks.task: Research a question and write a cited report

items.when: Before searching, to split the question into sub-questions and sources to find
When you want one guided run from outline to sources to a checked report
When each claim in the report must be checked against the exact source quote
When the topic is recent and the evidence is what people are saying this month
When the report is drafted, to check it claim by claim as you would anyone's draft

tasks.task: Check and format a reference list

items.when: When every citation must be real, correct and say what the text claims
When in-text citations must match the reference list and the cited papers
When the list is revised more than once and mismatches and duplicates keep returning
When the references live in Zotero and need tidying or export as citations

tasks.task: Check health, product or ad claims against the evidence

items.when: When a product page or deck makes claims that must each trace to a source
When the claims are about health, to sort each as validated, directional or unsupported
When ad or page copy needs each claim marked fine, needs proof or cut
When the client has supplied evidence, to see which claims go further than it allows
When the piece is a pitch or post and the missing context matters as much as the facts

tasks.task: Review the quality of a set of sources

items.when: When you must say which sources can carry a claim and which cannot
When you do not know who is behind a source, to research the publisher or author
When a source mixes reporting with argument, to separate what it shows from what it urges
When a source is persuasive and you have not yet asked how it could be wrong

tasks.task: Write reading notes or an annotated source list

items.when: For each source, to get its claims, evidence, gaps and the lines worth keeping
When a paper is dense, to find its main idea and the sections to read closely
When a folder of saved reading must become linked notes and a sourced answer
When the notes should end as one table the client can scan

tasks.task: Prepare a journal club or team briefing on one paper

items.when: When one paper must be explained to a team or board in 10 to 20 minutes
When you want to question the paper and your notes before writing the briefing
When slides and speaker notes must show figures that trace to the paper's tables
When the briefing is a formal talk and needs slides, notes and a script
Before the session, to read the briefing as the team would and list what they must ask

tasks.task: Run the monthly source and retraction watch

items.when: Monthly, for a client whose published content cites studies, statistics or reports
When a topic should be watched for new papers that change what the content says
When a cited source has moved, changed or been withdrawn and the reference must be fixed

tasks.task: Write a cultural brief for a new market or community

items.when: When the client will serve a community new to them and has notes and sources
When the notes are thin, to plan what to learn and map who already serves the community
When the offer is drafted, to review cultural fit and who it may shut out
When the offer was built for another market, to surface the assumptions baked into it

tasks.task: Plan a small field study and review field notes

items.when: When you need who to meet, a guide and how the notes will be read afterwards
When field notes are in, to rank themes by how often they come up, with quotes
When the notes describe behaviour, to map the beliefs behind it and test each on evidence
When the reviewed notes must become a brief the client can act on

tasks.task: Research the history of a business, trade or place

items.when: When old invoices, letters and photos must become a checked history
When the documents are scans and the text must be read with page positions
When names, dates and sums from a scan must be checked against the page
When the checked timeline should become a heritage story or an about page
Before the story is published, to mark each family legend that has no document behind it

tasks.task: Write a short background on an industry or craft

items.when: Before writing, to list what to cover and the questions to answer for each part
When the background must cover size, main players and how the trade is changing
When the client wants one page with every statement tied to a source

tasks.task: Write a research plan for one question

items.when: When the plan is a time-boxed review with a decision at the end
When the question is broad and needs sub-questions and what a good answer looks like
When the client has an observation, to turn it into testable guesses and rival explanations
When time is short, to compare a quick scan and a fuller review with cost and dates

tasks.task: Turn findings into a summary and slide text

items.when: When a finished report needs a summary, a slide brief and a fact-check list
When the reader has one page of time and needs the answer first
When the findings use research terms the named reader will not know
Before it is sent, to check nothing in the short version says more than the report does

tasks.task: Look up a fact in a public database or patent record

items.when: When you know the database and need the figure with its source and date
When the question is whether an idea is already patented or who holds patents in a field

always.when: Before any answer or report leaves, to tie each fact to a dated source or cut it
Before delivery, to catch typos, misspelt author names and one term used two ways

helpers.when: When the checked draft needs rewriting for flow and style, not only for facts
When the question is market size, rivals or demand, not what studies say
When the answer needs new interviews or surveys, not desk research
When the sources include raw data that must be analysed, not only read
When the briefing needs designed slides, not slide text and notes
When key sources are in a language the client cannot read

gaps: No library item checks whether a cited paper has been retracted, corrected or superseded
No library item grades a source on publisher, method, date and conflicts of interest
No library item formats a reference list in a named style such as APA, Harvard or Vancouver
No library item writes an annotated bibliography as its main job
No library item checks a quote and its attribution against the original
No library item writes a cultural brief for a community or plans an ethnographic field study
No library item builds a business or local history timeline from old documents or tests a family legend
No library item offers two or three ways to structure a journal club briefing to compare
No mind in the library is built on a historian or an anthropologist
No tool guide covers academic search tools such as Elicit, Consensus or Scite
